A1.8              | gap: not stated — depends on the trigger, which is itself unstated (A1.1)
A2.calculation.1  | Input: duration/cumulative-total values in ms. Output: a value truncated to the second. Rule — a total's displayed value = truncate(ms → s); a segment's displayed value = truncate(later cumulative total) − truncate(earlier cumulative total), never truncate(segment's own raw ms)
A2.calculation.2  | gap: block does not state what happens when a needed value is missing (e.g. no prior cumulative total for the first segment)
A2.calculation.3  | gap: block does not state the bounds or acceptable range of the output (e.g. can a segment display 0 seconds, can it be negative)
A4.1              | "Duration", "cumulative total" and "segment" are each used consistently with the functional role the block itself explains (durations in ms, cumulative total as a running sum, segment as the span between two cumulative totals) — none is an undefined self-reference
A4.2              | gap: "a delta is computed on millisecond values, then truncated only at display" — unclear whether "delta" designates the same segment computation already described (difference of two truncated totals) or a different computation entirely
A4.3              | No comparison-dependent qualifier found — "never by rounding" and "never by truncating the segment's own duration" each state the excluded alternative outright, nothing is left missing a term

Consumes  | duration values (ms), cumulative total values (ms)
Produces  | displayed duration truncated to the second (total); segment's displayed duration = difference of two truncated cumulative totals

Names     | duration = value stored in milliseconds; cumulative total = running sum of durations, truncated to the second for display; segment = span between two cumulative totals, displayed as the difference of their truncated values; delta = value computed on millisecond values then truncated only at display (referent unclear, see Q7)
